records.question: How many orders are there in total?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM orders_safe LIMIT 500

records.question: How many customers are there?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS total_customers FROM customers_safe LIMIT 500

records.question: What is the average order value?
records.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(total), 2) AS average_order_value FROM orders_safe WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2024-11-04' AND '2026-11-04' LIMIT 500
assumptions: Average order value is calculated using only completed and shipped orders (status IN ('completed', 'shipped'))
Time range is fixed to the full available dataset (2024-11-04 to 2026-11-04)

records.question: What is the highest order total?
records.sql: SELECT MAX(total) AS highest_order_total FROM orders_safe LIMIT 500

records.question: How many products are there?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) AS total_products FROM order_items_safe JOIN products_safe ON order_items_safe.product_id = products_safe.id LIMIT 500

records.question: How many orders were cancelled?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cancelled_orders_count FROM orders_safe WHERE status = 'cancelled' LIMIT 500

records.question: What is the price of the most expensive product?
records.sql: SELECT MAX(price) AS most_expensive_product_price FROM products_safe LIMIT 500

records.question: How many customers are in India?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count_in_india FROM customers_safe WHERE country = 'India' LIMIT 500

records.question: Number of customers per country
records.sql: SELECT country, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS customer_count FROM customers_safe GROUP BY country ORDER BY customer_count DESC LIMIT 500

records.question: Order count by status
records.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders_safe GROUP BY status ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 500

records.question: Total revenue by region
records.sql: SELECT region, SUM(total) AS total_revenue FROM orders_safe GROUP BY region ORDER BY region LIMIT 500

records.question: Average order value by region
records.sql: SELECT region, ROUND(AVG(orders_safe.total), 2) AS average_order_value FROM orders_safe GROUP BY region ORDER BY region LIMIT 500

records.question: How many products are in each category?
records.sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products_safe GROUP BY category ORDER BY product_count DESC LIMIT 500

records.question: How many customers are in each region?
records.sql: SELECT region, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS customer_count FROM customers_safe GROUP BY region ORDER BY region LIMIT 500

records.question: Average product price by category
records.sql: SELECT category, ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS average_product_price FROM products_safe GROUP BY category ORDER BY category LIMIT 500

records.question: Order count by region and status
records.sql: SELECT region, status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders_safe GROUP BY region, status ORDER BY region, status LIMIT 500

records.question: What is the maximum order total in each region?
records.sql: SELECT region, MAX(total) AS max_order_total FROM orders_safe GROUP BY region ORDER BY region LIMIT 500

records.question: Revenue by product category
records.sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.total) AS revenue FROM order_items_safe AS oi JOIN orders_safe AS o ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products_safe AS p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 500
assumptions: Revenue is calculated as the sum of order totals (SUM(o.total)) per product category
records.gold_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) FROM order_items_safe oi JOIN products_safe p ON p.id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category
records.detail: gold: 5 rows x 2 cols, got: 5 rows x 2 cols

records.question: Top 3 product categories by units sold
records.sql: WITH category_units AS (SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM order_items_safe AS oi JOIN products_safe AS p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC LIMIT 3) SELECT * FROM category_units LIMIT 500

records.question: Average order value by customer country
records.sql: SELECT c.country, ROUND(AVG(o.total), 2) AS average_order_value FROM customers_safe AS c JOIN orders_safe AS o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY average_order_value DESC LIMIT 500
assumptions: Average order value is calculated as the sum of order totals divided by the number of orders per customer country.
records.gold_sql: SELECT c.country, AVG(o.total) FROM orders_safe o JOIN customers_safe c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.country
records.detail: gold: 8 rows x 2 cols, got: 8 rows x 2 cols

records.question: How many customers have placed more than 6 orders?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers_with_more_than_6_orders FROM orders_safe WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders_safe GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 6) LIMIT 500

records.question: Revenue by region for the Electronics category
records.sql: SELECT o.region, SUM(o.total) AS electronics_revenue FROM orders_safe AS o JOIN order_items_safe AS oi ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products_safe AS p ON oi.product_id = p.id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' GROUP BY o.region ORDER BY o.region LIMIT 500
assumptions: Revenue is defined as SUM(total) from orders_safe
Electronics category is filtered by products_safe.category = 'Electronics'
records.gold_sql: SELECT o.region, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) FROM order_items_safe oi JOIN orders_safe o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products_safe p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' GROUP BY o.region
records.detail: gold: 3 rows x 2 cols, got: 3 rows x 2 cols

records.question: Top 5 customer IDs by total spend
records.sql: WITH customer_spend AS (SELECT c.id AS customer_id, SUM(o.total) AS total_spend FROM customers_safe AS c JOIN orders_safe AS o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id) SELECT customer_id, total_spend FROM customer_spend ORDER BY total_spend DESC LIMIT 5

records.question: Number of orders per customer country
records.sql: SELECT c.country, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count FROM customers_safe AS c JOIN orders_safe AS o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 500

records.question: Which product has the highest total revenue? Give only the product name.
records.sql: WITH product_revenue AS (SELECT p.name AS product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items_safe AS oi JOIN orders_safe AS o ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products_safe AS p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.name) SELECT product_name FROM product_revenue ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1

records.question: Total revenue from orders placed by customers in Germany
records.sql: SELECT SUM(o.total) AS total_revenue_germany FROM orders_safe AS o JOIN customers_safe AS c ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.country = 'Germany' LIMIT 500
assumptions: Revenue is defined as the sum of the 'total' column in orders_safe.

records.question: Monthly order count for 2025
records.sql: SELECT MONTH(order_date) AS month, YEAR(order_date) AS year, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders_safe WHERE YEAR(order_date) = 2025 GROUP BY MONTH(order_date), YEAR(order_date) ORDER BY MONTH(order_date) LIMIT 500

records.question: Total revenue in 2025
records.sql: SELECT SUM(orders_safe.total) AS total_revenue_2025 FROM orders_safe WHERE YEAR(order_date) = 2025 LIMIT 500

records.question: Quarterly order counts for 2025
records.sql: WITH quarterly_orders AS (SELECT QUARTER(order_date) AS quarter, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders_safe WHERE YEAR(order_date) = 2025 GROUP BY QUARTER(order_date) ORDER BY quarter) SELECT quarter, order_count, CONCAT('Q', quarter, ' 2025') AS quarter_label FROM quarterly_orders LIMIT 500
assumptions: Quarterly order counts refer to the number of rows in orders_safe grouped by quarter of the order_date

records.question: Total revenue by year
records.sql: WITH yearly_revenue AS (SELECT YEAR(order_date) AS year, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM orders_safe GROUP BY YEAR(order_date) ORDER BY year) SELECT * FROM yearly_revenue LIMIT 500
assumptions: Revenue is defined as the sum of the 'total' column in orders_safe

records.question: How many customers signed up in 2024?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS customers_signed_up_in_2024 FROM customers_safe WHERE YEAR(signup_date) = 2024 LIMIT 500

records.question: Customers who signed up in 2024, by region
records.sql: SELECT region, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS customer_count FROM customers_safe WHERE YEAR(signup_date) = 2024 GROUP BY region ORDER BY region LIMIT 500

records.question: Which month of 2025 had the highest revenue? Give the month number.
records.sql: SELECT MONTH(order_date) AS month_number, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM orders_safe WHERE YEAR(order_date) = 2025 GROUP BY MONTH(order_date) ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1
assumptions: Revenue is defined as the sum of the 'total' column in orders_safe

records.question: How many orders were placed in the second half of 2025?
records.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders_safe WHERE order_date >= '2025-07-01' AND order_date <= '2025-12-31'

records.question: Total revenue by region and year for 2025 and 2026
records.sql: WITH yearly_revenue AS (SELECT YEAR(o.order_date) AS year, o.region, SUM(o.total) AS total_revenue FROM orders_safe AS o WHERE YEAR(o.order_date) IN (2025, 2026) GROUP BY YEAR(o.order_date), o.region) SELECT year, region, ROUND(total_revenue, 2) AS total_revenue FROM yearly_revenue ORDER BY year, region LIMIT 500
assumptions: Revenue is defined as the sum of the 'total' column in orders_safe

records.question: How many customers have placed at least one refunded order?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS refunded_order_customers_count FROM orders_safe AS o WHERE o.status = 'refunded' LIMIT 500

records.question: What percentage of orders were cancelled?
records.sql: SELECT ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS percentage_cancelled_orders FROM orders_safe LIMIT 500

records.question: What is the total number of units sold?
records.sql: SELECT SUM(quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM order_items_safe LIMIT 500

records.question: How many orders have a total above 1000?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS high_value_orders_count FROM orders_safe WHERE total > 1000 LIMIT 500

records.question: What is the average order value for completed orders?
records.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(orders_safe.total), 2) AS average_order_value_completed FROM orders_safe WHERE status = 'completed' LIMIT 500
assumptions: Average order value is calculated as SUM(total) / COUNT(order_id) for completed orders only.
